The climate in Sliven

Sliven is about 270 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 31°C; the coldest is January, when nights average −1°C. Around 670 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in November (about 82 mm).

Sliven lies at the foot of the Blue Rocks in the eastern Balkan Mountains and is known for its wind: when cold air arrives from the north, a strong, gusty wind known as the Sliven bora comes down over the mountain. Summers are hot, and winters are milder than north of the Balkans. The nearby mountains bring more rain in autumn.
